original_hook: When $MTL plunged 15.26% toward its $0.263 intraday low, 1H volume on breakdown candles peaked at 582k and 501k units. But as price stabilized around $0.272, hourly turnover collapsed to just 49.6k units. Surface momentum looks heavy, but this 90% drop in turnover near the bottom suggests seller exhaustion rather than active distribution. Panic flushed leverage out early, leaving price in a low-volume drift. The catch: low volume at support can also mean zero buyer interest. Without bid depth, even a small market order could tear through thin support. 📊 MTL 1H: price $0.272 • support $0.263 • resistance $0.342 • TP1 $0.24325 • target $0.2235 • SL / invalidation $0.342 (short bias). Levels are chart-derived scenarios, not guarantees. Execution test: A 1H close above $0.282 on >200k volume confirms buy-side absorption. What confirmation on $MTL would make you treat this setup as real rather than an early headline move?
